description: Second discovery batch for new Brali Protocol candidates, focused on communication, creativity, work, digital wellbeing, and human-AI decision calibration. Research records do not bypass Evidence Decisions or protocol implementation gates.

research_candidates.title: Spoken disagreement is more constructive than written disagreement
research_candidates.review_notes: The full open-access article was reviewed. Across a series of randomized experiments, spoken disagreement produced greater perceived understanding and lower perceived conflict than written disagreement on average, with conversational receptiveness contributing to the pattern. The authors explicitly note low overall conflict levels, mostly student and stranger samples, controversial-opinion conversations rather than close-relationship or workplace disputes, and uncertainty about high-stakes or culturally indirect settings. Brali should therefore test a bounded 'move an important disagreement from text to voice' protocol, while excluding situations where documentation, safety, power imbalance, harassment, legal requirements, or deliberate asynchronous reflection make writing preferable.

research_candidates.title: The impact of walking on creative thinking: A systematic review and meta-analysis
research_candidates.review_notes: The full open-access systematic review and meta-analysis was reviewed. Twenty-three studies with roughly 1,036 participants were included; sensitivity analyses restricted to randomized studies still found a large positive effect of walking on divergent thinking. Evidence for divergent thinking was rated moderate certainty, while evidence for convergent thinking was very low certainty and did not show a clear effect. Heterogeneity remained substantial, most samples were post-secondary students, and many positive studies came from one research group. Brali should exploit the useful asymmetry: walk when the job is to generate alternatives, then switch context when the job becomes evaluation and selection. Do not claim that walking improves all creativity, reasoning, intelligence, or decision quality, and do not invent one optimal walking duration or intensity.

research_candidates.title: Smartphone screen time reduction improves mental health: a randomized controlled trial
research_candidates.review_notes: The full open-access randomized controlled trial was reviewed. Healthy students aged 18-29 who used smartphones at least three hours per day were randomized to three weeks of smartphone screen time at or below two hours per day or control. Small-to-medium short-term improvements were reported in several self-reported wellbeing outcomes, but the sample was small and non-representative, mental-health outcomes were self-report measures, total device substitution could not be ruled out, and smartphone use rapidly returned toward baseline after the intervention. Brali should not publish 'two hours is healthy' or a treatment claim. A safer research direction is a bounded digital-load experiment: deliberately lower smartphone time below personal baseline for a short period, measure actual usage and functional outcomes, then review what rebounds and why.

research_candidates.title: Strengths-based performance conversations: a randomized trial in the UK civil service
research_candidates.container_title: Journal of Organizational Effectiveness: People and Performance
research_candidates.review_notes: Fresh real-world work lead. The cluster-randomized trial involved two UK civil-service organizations, with 8,843 managerial and non-managerial subjects in the trial and 2,903 survey responses used in the impact evaluation. Training managers in a strengths-based performance-conversation approach improved employees' perceived usefulness of one-to-one meetings for learning and development; evidence for job-performance improvement was weak. This is not yet protocol-ready because the complete source still needs a Brali Evidence Decision. Candidate direction: redesign a 1:1 around where effective performance already occurs, what conditions enable it, and how to create more of those conditions, without promising higher performance.

research_candidates.title: Generative AI and Organizational Decision-Making: A Systematic Review of Performance Effects
research_candidates.review_notes: High-priority 2026 lead for Brali's people-and-agents positioning. The accessible source abstract reports a systematic review of 15 studies with 15,752 participants and proposes that uniformly confident AI outputs can impair human calibration of when to delegate. Reported aggregate effects differed by decision phase: positive in intelligence/information tasks, mixed in design, and negative in final choice. Treat these numerical effects as discovery-only until the complete paper is reviewed. Candidate protocol direction: explicitly separate 'expand the information or option set with AI' from 'make the final choice', and require independent checks before delegating consequential selection to a model.
